name: NEO-6M GPS module
description: u-blox NEO-6M GPS receiver on its common breakout (GY-NEO6MV2): NMEA sentences at 9600 baud once a second, a fix after the time to first fix while the antenna sees the sky, and the 1 Hz time pulse that blinks the board's LED. Position, altitude, speed, course, satellites in view and sky view are interactive inputs.

pins.name: VCC
pins.doc: Board supply, 3 to 5 V (an on-board 3.3 V regulator)

pins.name: RXD
pins.doc: UART in (UBX and NMEA commands: not modelled)

pins.name: TXD
pins.doc: UART out, NMEA at 3.3 V levels

pins.name: TIMEPULSE
pins.doc: 1 Hz time pulse, 100 ms, while fixed (the board's LED)

baud.doc: The UART rate the module was configured to (9600 out of the box)

start.doc: The start at power-up: cold (no almanac, 27 s), warm (27 s) or hot (recent fix kept by the backup battery, 1 s)

geoid_separation.doc: Geoid above the WGS84 ellipsoid at the place, m (GGA)

functional.claims: NMEA 0183 at `baud` 8N1 once a second from the top of the second: RMC, VTG, GGA, GSA, GSV and GLL with checksums, empty fields without a fix; the first fix after the data sheet's time to first fix (cold/warm 27 s, hot 1 s) with the sky in view and four satellites or more, lost without them and regained in 1 s; UTC from utc_start, ddmm.mmmmm coordinates, speed in knots and km/h, course, quality, satellites, HDOP, altitude and geoid separation; TIMEPULSE 100 ms at 1 Hz while fixed; silent below 2.7 V.
omissions: UBX binary messages and configuration commands on RXD (rate and messages stay as set)
the start-up $GPTXT banner
the position's noise and accuracy (2.5 m CEP)
UTC time known before the first fix
the satellites' real orbits (a fixed, plausible sky)
the backup battery's effect on the start (the start parameter sets it)
supply current
